status: flat-background quadratic pole census for the smallest reduced-metric curvature-square completion and softened-selector radial completion of claim 1596

domain.startingAction: the explicit MacDowell-Mansouri/Stelle-West plus torsion-square action of claim 1596
domain.orderOfOperations: solve the full-rank algebraic torsion equation first, then build curvature invariants from the resulting Levi-Civita curvature
domain.background: flat-space pole diagnostic after tuning the vacuum energy and selector tadpole; every claimed AdS application must repeat the background-dependent residue and stability analysis
domain.warning: a first-order R(omega)^2 Poincare-gauge theory is a larger action class and is not silently identified with this reduced-metric completion

curvatureSquareAction.action: S=sqrt(-g){(M_Pl^2/2)[R-2 Lambda+R^2/(6 m_0^2)]-(M_Pl^2/(4 m_2^2)) C_{mu nu rho sigma}C^{mu nu rho sigma}}
curvatureSquareAction.normalization: m_0 and m_2 are defined by the poles displayed below; the four-dimensional Euler density has been omitted because it has no local quadratic pole

decisions.finiteWeylSquared: ordinary Feynman quantization has an unavoidable negative-residue massive spin-2 pole; no sign choice makes both spin-2 residues positive
decisions.pureR2Line: the m_2 -> infinity line removes the Weyl pole and leaves the two massless graviton helicities plus one scalaron
decisions.extraMassless: m_0^2=0 is outside the displayed local parametrization and corresponds to loss of a finite positive scalar gap

scalaronAuxiliaryWitness.jordanIdentity: R+R^2/(6m_0^2) = Phi R-(3/2)m_0^2(Phi-1)^2 after eliminating Phi, with Phi=1+R/(3m_0^2)
scalaronAuxiliaryWitness.decision: the R^2 mode is a healthy gapped scalar for M_Pl^2>0 and m_0^2>0; it is not torsion and it is not a Yang-Mills mass gap

softenedSelector.radialInvariant: S_rad=-(Z/(8ell^2)) integral d(V^2) wedge star d(V^2)-integral U(V^2) star 1
softenedSelector.tuning: U(0) and U'(0) absorb the target cosmological constant and radial tadpole; define U''(0)=mu_rho^2
healthyConditions: M_Pl^2>0 and F(rho)>0 in the admitted field neighborhood
softenedSelector.decision: softening the norm can add one healthy gapped scalar, but its kinetic coefficient and potential curvature are new input parameters rather than predictions of Spin(2,3) or the minimal Stelle-West action

joinedSpectrum.healthyLocalSubspace: lambda not in {-1/2,1/4,2}, M_Pl^2>0, no finite Weyl-squared pole, m_0^2>0 when R^2 is present, and K_rho>0 with mu_rho^2>0 when the selector norm is softened
physicalModes: optional healthy scalaron of mass squared m_0^2
optional healthy selector-radial scalar of mass squared mu_rho^2/K_rho
joinedSpectrum.lenseThirring: the p^2=0 positive-residue spin-2 pole remains, so the infrared 1/r and gravitomagnetic response are not Yukawa removed
joinedSpectrum.nonemptyExample: lambda=0, M_Pl^2=ell^2=1, m_0^2=4, no Weyl-squared term, Z=1, mu_rho^2=5 gives two positive mixed-scalar masses squared (15-sqrt(145))/2 and (15+sqrt(145))/2, with no extra spin-2 pole

connectionToClaim1596.genericLambda: the reduced completion is defined only after the rank-24 torsion Hessian has been inverted
connectionToClaim1596.lambdaQuarter: the four-component axial block is degenerate
connectionToClaim1596.lambdaTwo: the four-component trace block is degenerate
connectionToClaim1596.decision: curvature-square or selector-radial terms do not license integrating through these singular surfaces; they require a separate first-order constraint analysis

exhaustionAndStopRules: REJECT every finite local Weyl-squared coefficient under ordinary Feynman pole quantization because its massive spin-2 residue is opposite to the graviton residue
ADMIT the local R+R^2 line at quadratic order only for M_Pl^2>0 and m_0^2>0
ADMIT the softened radial selector only where F>0, K_rho>0 and mu_rho^2>0
STOP at the three claim-1596 torsion degeneracies before algebraic reduction
DO NOT identify either scalar mass with a Yang-Mills mass gap or a torsion gap
REPEAT the calculation on AdS and on every claimed cosmological background; the flat witness is necessary but not sufficient

Radiative generation of a Weyl-squared counterterm means the tree-level healthy R^2 line is not by itself a closed quantum completion; fakeon, Lee-Wick or nonlocal prescriptions are different quantizations and require separate axioms
A genuine propagating first-order torsion extension requires the full parity-even Poincare-gauge spin-projector analysis and is outside this reduced minimal class
decision: The minimal propagating extension is not empty: a pure R^2 scalaron and/or a softened selector radial mode can be healthy and gapped while the graviton stays massless. But a finite local Weyl-squared term fails by an exact opposite-residue spin-2 pole, and none of these modes realizes a torsion gap. This exhausts the reduced-metric plus single-radial local quadratic extension.
